verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call the community together and to tell the camps when to move.
When both trumpets are blown, the whole community must gather in front of you at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of the army groups of Israel, must gather in front of you.
When the trumpets sound a loud alarm, the tribes camped on the east side must set out.
When the alarm sounds a second time, the tribes camped on the south side must set out. The alarm will be the signal to move.
But when you call the people together, blow the trumpets without sounding the alarm.
Aaron's sons, the priests, will blow the trumpets. This is a rule forever for you and for all your families to come.
When you go to war in your own land against an enemy who attacks you, sound the alarm on the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you and save you from your enemies.

Also on your happy days, at your special feasts, and at the start of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. They will remind your God of you. I am the LORD your God."
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the Tent of the Covenant Law.
Then the people of Israel set out from the Sinai desert and travelled from place to place, until the cloud stopped in the desert of Paran.
This was the first time they set out at the LORD's command through Moses.
First, the army groups under the flag of Judah's camp set out. Nahshon son of Amminadab was over this army.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the army of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was over the army of the tribe of Zebulun.
Then the Holy Tent was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.
Next, the army groups under the flag of Reuben's camp set out. Elizur son of Shedeur was over this army.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the army of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the army of the tribe of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The Holy Tent was set up again before they arrived.
Next, the army groups under the flag of Ephraim's camp set out. Elishama son of Ammihud was over this army.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the army of the tribe of Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni was over the army of the tribe of Benjamin.
Last of all, the army groups under the flag of Dan's camp set out, guarding the back of all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over this army.
Pagiel son of Ochran was over the army of the tribe of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan was over the army of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order in which the army groups of Israel marched when they set out.

Moses said to Hobab, son of Moses' father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, "We are setting out for the place the LORD said he would give us. Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
But Hobab answered, "No, I will not go. I am going back to my own land and my own people."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the desert, and you can be our guide.
If you come with us, we will share with you all the good things the LORD gives us."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and travelled for three days. The Covenant Box of the LORD went ahead of them during those three days, to find them a place to rest.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the Covenant Box set out, Moses said, "Rise up, LORD! Let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you run away from you!"
And whenever it stopped, he said, "Come back, LORD, to the many thousands of Israel."
